record.what_it_does: Email marketing platform: audiences, campaigns, automations, ecommerce; Mandrill for transactional email.
record.auth_notes: Marketing API: the OAuth 2 authorization code flow uses a client_id and client_secret from the Registered Apps page. With an API key you call the API as yourself: either HTTP Basic auth (`anystring:<apikey>`) or passing the key as a token in the client libraries. The data center comes from the API key suffix or, for OAuth, from the metadata endpoint. Transactional (Mandrill) has a separate API key, sent as a Bearer header to its MCP. Marketing API limit: 10 simultaneous connections per user. That limit cannot be raised.
record.access_notes: Any Mailchimp account can register an OAuth app on the Registered Apps page and get a client_id and client_secret. The OAuth guide lists only "a Mailchimp account" as a prerequisite and mentions no app review. The compare-plans page shows integrations as "Included" on Free. It has no explicit Marketing API row, so free-plan API access is implied but not stated. Transactional (Mandrill) is "Demo only" on Free and needs a paid add-on to send.
record.api_breadth_notes: Marketing API v3.0 at api.mailchimp.com/3.0 covers lists/audiences, members, campaigns, automations, templates, reports, ecommerce, landing pages, batch operations and webhooks. That is well over 100 operations, though I did not count them exactly. The Transactional API is separate.
record.mcp_notes: Two vendor-hosted MCP servers are documented, but neither gives access to Marketing account data. (1) https://mailchimp.com/developer/_mcp/server searches documentation only and needs no auth. (2) https://mandrillapp.com/mcp is the Transactional MCP, authenticated with a Bearer Mandrill API key. Mailchimp also ships a first-party Claude connector: the help article says to "Sign in with your Intuit Mailchimp account" from Claude's Connectors list. A ChatGPT app also exists. The hosted endpoint ai-inc.mailchimp.com/claude/mcp/v2 appears only in third-party directories. Mailchimp's docs do not document it as open to arbitrary MCP clients. Community servers (mailchimp-mcp, mcp-mailchimp, damientilman/mailchimp-mcp-server) use an API key.
record.blocker_notes: The REST API is broad, with an OpenAPI spec, self-serve OAuth registration, and no documented review. The 10-connection-per-user cap matters for heavy concurrent agent use.

evidence.quote: Registering gives you the `client_id` and `client_secret` your server needs.
This is the only time you'll be able to see `client_secret`, so you'll need to copy it and store it securely.
We use the OpenAPI Specification (formerly known as Swagger) to describe each endpoint.
The Marketing API has a limit of 10 simultaneous connections.
You can also create list webhooks programmatically via the API.
This searches documentation, not your Mailchimp account.
Our MCP specifically allows you to interact with the Transactional Messaging API.
Sign in with your Intuit Mailchimp account when prompted.

record.needs_human: Mailchimp's pricing page does not state that the Free plan includes Marketing API access. It only shows integrations as "Included". Someone should create a key on a free account to confirm. Also unconfirmed: whether the Claude connector's MCP endpoint (reportedly ai-inc.mailchimp.com/claude/mcp/v2) accepts third-party clients.
